description: Child knows individual letter sounds but cannot blend them into syllables — says 's-o-l' but cannot produce 'sol'. Exercise uses continuous blending modelled by teacher — elongating each sound and sliding into next without pause.
child_instruction: Dis le son sans t'arrêter entre les lettres. Fais-les glisser!

description: Child cannot blend consonant-vowel pairs into syllables. Exercise uses the stretching rope technique — child holds a physical rope and stretches it while saying first sound, then snaps together while blending into syllable.
child_instruction: Étire la corde pour le premier son. Claque pour faire la syllabe!

description: Child knows vowel sounds but cannot blend a consonant onto a vowel to make a CV syllable — says 's' and 'a' separately but cannot produce 'sa'. Exercise uses the snake technique — teacher makes a long hissing 's' sound and the child gradually opens their mouth to add 'a', producing 'sa' as a continuous sound without a break.
child_instruction: Fais le son du serpent ssss... et ouvre doucement la bouche pour ajouter 'a'. Ssssa!

description: Child can produce individual phonemes correctly but pauses completely between each one — segmented reading with no flow. Exercise uses rhythmic blending — child claps a slow steady rhythm while saying each phoneme on a beat, then gradually speeds up the rhythm until the phonemes flow together naturally.
child_instruction: Dis un son par battement. Accélère le rythme jusqu'à ce que ça coule.

description: Child cannot blend three-phoneme CVC words — knows each phoneme separately but cannot fuse them into a single syllable. Says 's... o... l' with clear pauses but cannot produce 'sol' as one unit. Exercise uses Elkonin boxes — three boxes drawn for each CVC word, child pushes a token into each box while saying each phoneme, then sweeps all tokens together with one continuous gesture while blending the word.
child_instruction: Pousse un jeton pour chaque son. Maintenant fais-les glisser ensemble d'un seul coup!

description: Child struggles to blend consonant clusters — reads CR as C + R separately. Exercise isolates common clusters (br/cr/dr/fr/gr/pr/tr) with picture anchors and progressive blending: sounds → cluster → word.
child_instruction: Apprends le groupe. Puis lis le mot entier.

description: Child can blend CV but not VC combinations — reads 'al' as two separate sounds but 'la' correctly. Exercise targets VC syllables specifically — vowel-final consonant pairs like 'al', 'el', 'in', 'on' are presented as chunks. Child practises until each VC chunk is automatic before encountering them in words.
child_instruction: Ces deux lettres font un seul son ensemble. Répète jusqu'à ce que ce soit automatique.

description: Child struggles to blend four-phoneme CCVC words — reads 'bras' letter by letter. Exercise uses a building pyramid — child blends the innermost consonant cluster first (ra), then adds the initial consonant (bra), then confirms it matches the written word. Builds the word from inside out.
child_instruction: D'abord lis le groupe 'ra'. Ajoute le 'b' devant: 'bra'. Maintenant lis le mot entier.

description: Child reads letter by letter without blending — extremely slow with no fluency. Exercise uses chunked word cards — whole syllable chunks shown rather than individual letters, forcing blend-first reading rather than letter-by-letter decoding.
child_instruction: Lis chaque bloc d'un seul coup. Ne décode pas lettre par lettre.

description: Child shows blending difficulty specifically with vowel digraphs — au/eau/ou — treating them as two separate sounds. Exercise builds digraph recognition through word family sorting — child groups words sharing the same digraph before reading.
child_instruction: Groupe les mots qui ont le même groupe de lettres. Puis lis.

description: Child blends simple words but loses the first phoneme when encountering longer words — 'lapin' becomes 'apin' because the child moves to the blend before completing the first phoneme. Exercise uses anchor-and-blend — child holds the first phoneme sound for two full seconds before blending forward.
child_instruction: Tiens le premier son deux secondes: 'llll...' puis glisse vers la suite.

description: Child can blend monosyllabic words but breaks down completely on two-syllable blending — reads each syllable correctly in isolation but cannot fuse them. Exercise uses syllable handshake — child says first syllable with left hand, second with right hand, then brings hands together while producing the full blended word.
child_instruction: Main gauche = première syllabe, main droite = deuxième. Applaudis pour fusionner!

description: Child has significant blending difficulties affecting reading fluency — reads at phoneme level only, producing very slow disconnected reading. Exercise uses repeated reading with a model — listens to fluent model three times, then reads independently.
child_instruction: Écoute 3 fois. Puis lis seul(e) à voix haute.

description: Child cannot blend morphologically complex words — separates affixes from roots incorrectly during reading. Exercise builds morphological blending — child identifies root, prefix, suffix separately then blends complete word.
child_instruction: Trouve: préfixe + racine + suffixe. Maintenant lis le mot entier.

description: Child can blend at word level but loses blending when reading in sentences — reverts to letter-by-letter decoding mid-sentence when encountering an unfamiliar word. Exercise uses sight word preparation — unknown words in the upcoming passage are practiced in isolation first, reducing the blending demand during connected reading.
child_instruction: Apprends ces mots difficiles avant de lire le texte. Ils apparaîtront dans la lecture.

description: Child has multiple simultaneous reading errors — blending, letter reversal, and vowel substitution — producing severely disrupted reading. Exercise uses supported oral reading with immediate corrective feedback only for errors affecting meaning.
child_instruction: Lis à voix haute. Je te corrige seulement si le sens change.

description: Severe blending difficulty at sentence level — child loses meaning of sentence while decoding individual words. Exercise uses phrase-level fluency building — child reads pre-chunked phrases as single units, never individual words.
child_instruction: Lis chaque phrase d'un seul souffle. Garde le sens en tête.

description: Child has severe blending difficulty at phoneme level — cannot decode even familiar words reliably. Exercise uses nonsense word reading for automaticity — child reads lists of phonetically regular but meaningless words like 'vabou', 'trelin', 'chospu'. Because the words are not real, the child cannot rely on memory or context and must genuinely decode each one phonologically. Timed sessions build decoding speed.
child_instruction: Ces mots n'existent pas — tu dois les décoder lettre par lettre. Lis aussi vite que tu peux.

description: Severe blending difficulty with complex multisyllabic words — scientific or geographic terms with five or more syllables cannot be decoded. Exercise uses morphological decomposition before blending — child identifies prefix, root, suffix of each complex word, blends each morpheme separately, then chains them together.
child_instruction: Découpe: préfixe + racine + suffixe. Lis chaque partie. Enchaîne les parties.

description: Persistent blending difficulty at sentence level — child loses sentence meaning while decoding individual words, reading in a slow monotone that prevents comprehension. Exercise uses prosodic reading support — stress marks, rhythm bars, and pause symbols are printed above the text. Child reads following the prosodic markers, which naturally chunks the text into meaningful units and maintains sentence-level blending flow.
child_instruction: Suis les marques au-dessus du texte: accent fort, barre de rythme, pause. Lis avec la mélodie.

description: Child transposes letters within simple words — reading 'sol' as 'slo' or 'par' as 'pra'. Exercise uses letter tiles that child physically rearranges to form correct word order. Hands-on manipulation before oral reading.
child_instruction: Arrange les lettres dans le bon ordre pour faire le mot.

description: Child reverses the order of two adjacent letters in reading. Exercise uses sliding window — child uncovers letters one at a time from left to right, preventing whole-word guessing and forcing sequential letter processing.
child_instruction: Découvre les lettres une par une de gauche à droite.

description: Child reverses two-letter consonant sequences — reading 'or' as 'ro' or 'en' as 'ne'. Exercise uses directional arrow cards — each two-letter sequence is printed with a left-to-right arrow underneath. Child traces the arrow before reading the sequence.
child_instruction: Suis la flèche de gauche à droite. Maintenant lis les deux lettres dans ce sens.

description: Child reverses the order of letters in their own name and other high-frequency words. Exercise uses word configuration boxes — the outline shape of the correctly-spelled word is shown, and child must fill in letters in order to match the shape. Familiar words build the concept of fixed letter order.
child_instruction: Remplis les cases pour que le mot ait la bonne forme. Lis-le ensuite.

description: Child transposes consonant cluster letters — reading 'bras' as 'bars', 'trop' as 'topr'. Exercise focuses on consonant cluster sequencing with visual arrow cues showing correct letter reading direction within clusters.
child_instruction: Suis les flèches pour lire les lettres dans le bon ordre.

description: Child reverses syllable order in two-syllable words — reading 'maison' as 'sonmai'. Exercise uses syllable ordering tasks — written syllables on separate cards, child orders them correctly then reads the assembled word.
child_instruction: Mets les syllabes dans le bon ordre. Lis le mot.

description: Child transposes the vowel and final consonant in CVC words — reading 'bal' as 'bla' or 'mar' as 'mra'. Exercise uses phoneme position practice — child is given the phonemes orally and must arrange magnetic letters in correct order before reading the assembled word.
child_instruction: Arrange les lettres magnétiques dans le bon ordre. Puis lis le mot.

description: Child reverses the order of the two letters in common digraphs — reading 'ch' as 'hc' or 'ou' as 'uo'. Exercise teaches digraphs as indivisible units — each digraph is presented as a single colour block that cannot be split. Child reads the block as one sound without internal letter-by-letter processing.
child_instruction: Ce bloc de couleur fait UN seul son. Lis-le d'un coup.

description: Child shows consistent left-to-right directionality errors in reading — starting from the right side of a word, reading from the middle outward, or scanning the line in a non-linear pattern. This is a visual tracking difficulty rather than a phonological sequencing problem. Exercise builds left-to-right tracking with a finger pointer and a reading window card that exposes text strictly from left to right, preventing the child from accessing any part of the word before reaching it.
child_instruction: Utilise ta fenêtre de lecture. Déplace-la de gauche à droite sans regarder devant.

description: Child transposes letters in medial position of three-letter clusters — reading 'str' as 'tsr'. Exercise isolates consonant cluster reading with repeated exposure and rhythm — child taps rhythm while reading cluster sequences.
child_instruction: Frappe le rythme pendant que tu lis le groupe de lettres.

description: Child reverses letters specifically in the second syllable of two-syllable words — first syllable is read correctly, second contains the transposition error. Exercise uses two-pass reading — child reads only the first syllable and stops, then reads only the second syllable alone, then reads the whole word.
child_instruction: Lis la 1ère syllabe → stop. Lis la 2ème syllabe → stop. Maintenant lis tout.

description: Child reverses letters and confuses b/d simultaneously — misreading 'drobe' as 'borbd'. Exercise uses multisensory approach — child traces letters on textured surface while naming them, then blends into word.
child_instruction: Trace la lettre en la nommant. Maintenant lis le mot.

description: Frequent letter transpositions within words during fluent reading, causing significant decoding errors. Exercise uses error-detection passages — child reads and marks words that look like they have letters in wrong order, then self-corrects.
child_instruction: Trouve les mots où les lettres semblent dans le mauvais ordre.

description: Child reverses letter sequences particularly in morphological endings — confusing -tion/-toin, -ment/-mnet. Exercise builds morphological pattern recognition through categorization of word endings before fluency reading.
child_instruction: Classe les mots selon leur terminaison. Puis lis-les.

description: Child transposes letters at morpheme boundaries — reversing the junction between root and suffix — reading 'portant' as 'portnat' or 'chantions' as 'chantinos'. This error is specific to the boundary position and suggests the child processes root and suffix as two separate sequences without integrating them. Exercise builds morpheme boundary awareness — child draws a vertical line between root and suffix before reading.
child_instruction: Trace une ligne entre la racine et la terminaison. Puis lis chaque partie.

description: Frequent transposition errors in academic text reading — scientific or historical vocabulary contains many unfamiliar letter sequences that the child reverses. Exercise uses preview vocabulary reading — child reads every polysyllabic content word in isolation before reading the full passage.
child_instruction: Lis d'abord les mots difficiles encadrés. Puis lis le texte entier.

description: Severe letter reversal and transposition across all positions in words, combined with slow reading speed. Exercise uses repeated reading with graphomotor reinforcement — child reads passage, rewrites key words in order, reads again.
child_instruction: Lis → Écris → Relis. Compare tes deux lectures.

description: Severe and persistent letter transposition across all word positions at extended text level. Exercise uses anagram detection — passage contains real words alongside anagram errors. Child identifies anagrams and corrects them before reading each paragraph.
child_instruction: Trouve les mots dont les lettres sont dans le mauvais ordre. Corrige, puis lis.

description: Child has automatized letter reversal patterns — the wrong letter order is read faster than the correct order, suggesting deep orthographic errors. Exercise uses deliberate slow reading — child reads each word at half normal speed with a physical token moving under each letter, forcing conscious sequential processing.
child_instruction: Déplace le jeton sous chaque lettre lentement. Ne lis pas vite.

description: Letter reversal errors combined with b/d confusion producing complex misreadings at paragraph level. Exercise integrates reversal and visual confusion strategies — child uses a combined reference card covering both error types and marks all target letters before reading any paragraph.
child_instruction: Utilise ta carte combinée. Marque les lettres difficiles avant de lire.

description: Child omits syllables in two-syllable words — reading 'papillon' as 'paillon' or 'chocolat' as 'choclat'. Exercise uses syllable clapping — child claps the number of syllables in the written word before reading, then reads ensuring the clap count matches the syllables produced. Visual colour blocks reinforce syllable boundaries.
child_instruction: Frappe dans tes mains pour chaque syllabe. Combien y en a-t-il?

description: Child drops final unstressed syllables specifically — reading 'fenêtre' as 'fenêt', 'table' as 'tab', or 'livre' as 'liv'. This pattern differs from general syllable omission because the child consistently preserves the first syllable and drops the end. Exercise uses final syllable highlighting — the last syllable of each word is printed in a different colour. Child must read to the colour boundary without stopping.
child_instruction: Lis jusqu'à la couleur différente. Ne t'arrête pas avant!

description: Child omits the first syllable of two-syllable words — reading 'maison' as 'son' or 'bateau' as 'teau'. This pattern suggests the child is guessing from word endings. Exercise uses first-syllable emphasis — the first syllable of each word is printed larger and bolder than the rest, requiring the child to start there.
child_instruction: Commence toujours par la grosse syllabe. Ne saute pas le début!

description: Child omits syllables inconsistently in two-syllable words — sometimes correct, sometimes not. Exercise uses syllable counting verification — after reading each word aloud, child counts on fingers whether the number of syllables they said matches the written word. Mismatch triggers a second attempt.
child_instruction: Lis le mot, puis compte sur tes doigts. Le nombre correspond?

description: Child omits medial syllables in three-syllable words — 'papillon' read as 'paillon'. Exercise builds syllable awareness through picture segmentation — pictures of familiar words are cut into syllable pieces that child must assemble.
child_instruction: Assemble les pièces du mot dans le bon ordre.

description: Child adds extra syllables in reading — epenthesis — inserting a vowel between consonant clusters. Exercise uses tapping and movement to map written syllables to produced syllables, then checks against the written form.
child_instruction: Lis le mot syllabe par syllabe. Compte et vérifie.

description: Child omits the medial syllable in three-syllable compound words — reading 'porte-manteau' as 'porte-teau'. Exercise uses syllable blocking — each syllable is printed in a separate physical block that the child must touch before saying its sound. No block may be skipped.
child_instruction: Touche chaque bloc avant de dire la syllabe. Ne passe pas de bloc!

description: Child omits syllables when the omitted syllable is phonologically weak — unstressed, short, or containing a schwa. Words like 'rapidement' lose the '-de-' or 'seulement' loses '-le-'. Exercise specifically targets schwa syllables — child marks every schwa syllable before reading to prevent omission.
child_instruction: Marque d'un point chaque syllabe faible avant de lire. Puis lis tout.

description: Child omits syllables specifically in polysyllabic words of 3-4 syllables, reading only beginning and end. Exercise uses syllable ladders — child reads the word adding one syllable at a time: 'pa' → 'pa-pi' → 'pa-pi-llon'.
child_instruction: Construis le mot une syllabe à la fois.

description: Child omits syllables under time pressure or in connected text but reads correctly in isolation. Exercise uses chunked reading — sentences are presented with explicit syllable boundaries marked. Child reads at slow pace with boundaries, then without.
child_instruction: Lis lentement avec les traits. Maintenant sans les traits.

description: Child omits syllables specifically in verb conjugations — reading 'mangeons' as 'mangons' or 'chantaient' as 'chantait'. This causes grammatical errors in reading. Exercise builds verb morphology awareness — child underlines the conjugation ending before reading the verb form.
child_instruction: Souligne la terminaison du verbe avant de le lire. Lis la terminaison en entier.

description: Child omits syllables in words with consecutive consonant clusters — reading 'abstrait' as 'abstrit' (dropping the vowel syllable within the cluster) or 'entreprise' as 'entrise' (dropping '-pre-'). The omitted syllable is always the one embedded in or adjacent to a consonant cluster. Exercise uses syllable bridge — child reads each consonant cluster as a bridge between syllables, explicitly connecting the final consonant of one syllable to the beginning of the next.
child_instruction: Les consonnes difficiles sont un pont entre les syllabes. Lis en passant le pont.

description: Frequent syllable omission in fluent reading causing significant comprehension problems. Exercise uses echo reading — teacher reads a sentence, child immediately echoes it matching syllables. Then child reads alone while teacher counts syllables.
child_instruction: Répète ce que j'ai lu, puis lis seul(e).

description: Child omits syllables in morphologically complex words — dropping suffixes like '-tion', '-ment' — causing grammatical errors. Exercise builds morphological awareness — child identifies root and suffix before reading full word.
child_instruction: Trouve la racine du mot. Maintenant lis le mot entier.

description: Frequent syllable omission in reading aloud for an audience — errors increase significantly under social pressure compared to reading alone. Exercise uses systematic rehearsal before performance — child reads passage silently first marking any word with more than two syllables, then reads aloud twice before the final performance.
child_instruction: Étape 1: marque les mots longs. Étape 2: lis deux fois. Étape 3: lis pour la classe.

description: Child omits syllables in reading comprehension tasks — the omissions change word meaning enough to cause comprehension errors. Exercise uses meaning verification — after reading each sentence, child selects the correct picture or definition confirming they read the key word correctly.
child_instruction: Lis la phrase. Maintenant montre l'image qui correspond au sens.

description: Complex multi-error profile with syllable omission, vowel substitution, and slow processing speed. Exercise uses prosodic reading — child reads with exaggerated sentence rhythm and stress, which naturally enforces correct syllable count and vowel duration.
child_instruction: Lis avec une belle mélodie. Marque bien les syllabes importantes.

description: Severe and frequent syllable omission across all word lengths affecting both reading and spelling. Exercise combines reading fluency with written dictation — child reads passage aloud, then writes key words from memory, checking syllable completeness.
child_instruction: Lis, puis écris les mots soulignés de mémoire.

description: Child omits syllables across all word lengths in extended text — the error rate is high enough to prevent accurate comprehension of grade-level material. Exercise uses assisted reading with audio support — child follows along as a recording plays, tracking each syllable. Then reads the same passage independently.
child_instruction: Écoute et suis avec ton doigt. Puis lis seul(e) le même texte.

description: Severe syllable omission combined with fast guessing — child produces plausible but incorrect words by omitting middle syllables. Exercise uses impossible word detection — passage contains a mix of real and impossibly-syllabified words. Child must flag any word that does not sound like a real French word.
child_instruction: Certains mots sont faux. Signale-les avec un X et dis comment ils devraient sonner.

description: The child confuses the letters b and d when reading simple CVC words like 'bal' and 'dal'. The exercise shows large isolated letters b and d side by side and asks the child to point to the correct one when the teacher says the sound. Visual cues and colour coding help distinguish the two letters.
child_instruction: Regarde les lettres. Montre-moi la lettre 'b'.

description: Child reverses b and d in very short words. Exercise uses the hand trick — left hand makes 'b', right hand makes 'd' — with simple one-syllable words. Child traces the letters with their finger before reading.
child_instruction: Utilise tes mains pour retrouver la lettre. Lis le mot.

description: Child cannot distinguish b from d even when letters are presented in isolation. Exercise uses a body anchor — child forms the letter with their whole body: arms out for 'b', arms back for 'd'. Physical movement creates a kinesthetic memory distinct from visual memory alone.
child_instruction: Fais la lettre avec ton corps. Bras devant = b. Bras derrière = d.

description: Child consistently writes and reads b as d in single letter recognition tasks. Exercise uses a verbal anchor — 'le b a un ventre à droite, le d a un ventre à gauche' — with a self-check rhyme the child repeats before writing or reading each letter.
child_instruction: Dis la comptine avant de lire: 'b a le ventre à droite, d a le ventre à gauche'.

description: Child confuses b/d and also struggles to blend them into words — double difficulty of letter identification and phoneme blending. Exercise separates the two problems: first identify the letter visually, then blend the word.
child_instruction: Étape 1: C'est un b ou un d? Étape 2: Maintenant lis le mot.

description: Child substitutes b for d in short reading passages. Exercise presents minimal pairs like 'bal/dal' and 'bon/don' with pictures. Child must select the picture matching the written word, forcing attention to the b/d distinction in context. Both words in each pair are real French words, preventing guessing from meaning alone.
child_instruction: Lis le mot et montre l'image qui correspond.

description: Child confuses p and q in reading. Exercise uses word recognition cards with highlighted ascenders and descenders. Child sorts words into b/d/p/q categories using physical card manipulation before reading aloud.
child_instruction: Trie les cartes selon la lettre que tu vois.

description: Child confuses b and d in consonant-vowel-consonant words but succeeds with isolated letters. Exercise uses progressive text exposure — words are revealed letter by letter from left to right on a screen. The child must say the letter sound before the next one appears, preventing whole-word guessing.
child_instruction: Dis le son de chaque lettre au fur et à mesure qu'elle apparaît.

description: Child confuses b and d within two-syllable words causing misreadings like 'domine' read as 'bomine'. Exercise uses cloze sentences where child must choose correct word from b/d minimal pair to make the sentence meaningful.
child_instruction: Choisis le bon mot pour compléter la phrase.

description: Child confuses m and n in reading — misreading 'ami' as 'ani', 'main' as 'nain', or 'maman' as 'naman'. Both letters have similar vertical strokes and differ only in the number of humps. Exercise uses visual counting strategy — child counts the humps in each letter before reading, then applies to simple words containing m and n.
child_instruction: Compte les bosses de la lettre. Maintenant lis le mot.

description: Child confuses b and d in two-syllable words when reading a list — errors increase with fatigue. Exercise uses strategic placement — b/d words are embedded in a list of non-b/d words. Child marks each b/d word before reading the full list, building sustained attention to the target letters.
child_instruction: Avant de lire, entoure tous les mots avec b ou d. Puis lis la liste.

description: Child shows b/d confusion specifically at the beginning of words but not mid-word. Exercise isolates word-initial position — words are presented with the first letter in a box. Child identifies only the boxed letter before reading the full word.
child_instruction: Regarde d'abord la lettre dans la boîte. C'est un b ou un d? Maintenant lis le mot.

description: Child shows persistent b/d confusion in fluent reading of multi-syllabic words, slowing reading speed significantly. Exercise uses timed word recognition with b/d words at sentence level. Child reads sentences aloud with audio feedback.
child_instruction: Lis la phrase à voix haute le plus vite possible.

description: Child confuses multiple mirror letter pairs simultaneously — b/d and p/q — in paragraph reading. Exercise uses color-coded paragraphs where each letter type appears in a distinct colour, helping child track visually while reading for meaning.
child_instruction: Lis le texte. Les lettres spéciales sont colorées pour t'aider.

description: Child confuses b and d in fluent connected reading causing word substitutions that change sentence meaning — 'le bébé dort' read as 'le dédé dort'. Exercise uses semantic checking — child reads each sentence and raises a hand if the meaning seems odd, then self-corrects the b/d word.
child_instruction: Lève la main si la phrase ne fait pas de sens. Trouve et corrige le mot.

description: Child confuses b, d, p, q simultaneously at sentence level — multiple substitution errors per sentence. Exercise uses a four-quadrant reference card — child keeps the card visible while reading a paragraph and consults it before reading any word containing these letters.
child_instruction: Utilise ta carte de référence pour chaque mot avec b, d, p ou q.

description: Advanced visual confusion — child confuses b/d/p/q simultaneously in extended reading with no visual supports. Exercise presents unsupported grade-level text and asks child to highlight all b-words before reading aloud. Builds automaticity.
child_instruction: Surligne tous les mots avec la lettre 'b', puis lis le texte.

description: Child shows persistent b/d/p/q confusion at paragraph level with no supports available. Exercise uses timed repeated reading — child reads a grade-level paragraph three times, counting b/d/p/q errors each time. Error count should decrease across repetitions, building automaticity through repetition.
child_instruction: Lis le texte 3 fois. Compte tes erreurs de b, d, p, q à chaque lecture.

description: Child has automatized incorrect b/d readings — errors are fast and confident, suggesting the wrong association is deeply ingrained. Exercise uses inhibition training — child reads a list of b/d words where the word is printed in a colour that conflicts with its meaning, forcing controlled processing over automatic response.
child_instruction: Lis le mot écrit, pas la couleur. Concentre-toi bien.

description: Advanced b/d/p/q confusion with slow reading rate and high error density in extended unsupported text. Exercise uses partner reading — child reads aloud to a partner who taps the table silently each time a b/d/p/q word appears. Child self-monitors at each tap before continuing.
child_instruction: Ton partenaire tapera pour chaque mot b/d/p/q. Vérifie avant de continuer.

description: Child substitutes simple vowel sounds, reading 'o' as 'ou' or vice versa in simple CVC words. Exercise uses picture-word matching with sound buttons — child hears the word and must select the written vowel they heard from two options.
child_instruction: Écoute le mot. Appuie sur la bonne voyelle.

description: Child confuses the sounds 'o' (as in 'mot') and 'ou' (as in 'mou') — both are round vowels differing only in lip aperture. This is one of the most common vowel reading errors in French dyslexia. Exercise uses mirror practice — child watches their lip shape for each sound — then identifies the correct written vowel after hearing the word in minimal pairs like 'mot/mou', 'sol/soul', 'col/cou'.
child_instruction: Regarde ta bouche dans le miroir. Quel son entends-tu? Montre la bonne voyelle.

description: Child reads 'i' as 'e' or vice versa in simple words — reading 'lit' as 'let' or 'sel' as 'sil'. Both are high front vowels differing only in height. Exercise uses mouth position cards — child places fingers on cheeks to feel the difference in mouth shape, then selects the correct written vowel.
child_instruction: Pose tes doigts sur tes joues. Quel son fait ta bouche? Montre la bonne voyelle.

description: Child substitutes 'a' for 'e' in simple CVC words — reading 'mer' as 'mar' or 'sel' as 'sal'. Exercise uses colour coding — all 'a' vowels appear in red, all 'e' vowels in blue across the exercise set. Child must name the colour before saying the vowel sound.
child_instruction: Quelle couleur vois-tu? Rouge = 'a', bleu = 'e'. Dis le son.

description: Child reads 'an' as 'a' or 'in' as 'i' in nasal vowel contexts, losing the nasal quality. Exercise uses minimal pair discrimination — child hears two pronunciations and must identify which is correct for the written word.
child_instruction: Quel son entends-tu? Entoure le bon.

description: Child substitutes ou/u confusion — reading 'tu' as 'tou' — a common Moroccan French phonetic interference. Exercise focuses on lip rounding contrast with mirror practice and word sorting by vowel type.
child_instruction: Regarde ta bouche dans le miroir. Dis le mot correctement.

description: Child confuses 'in' and 'un' — both nasal vowels that are phonetically merged in most French regional varieties, making them nearly impossible to distinguish by sound alone. Exercise focuses on grapheme recognition — child sorts word cards by their written nasal vowel group without reading aloud first.
child_instruction: Classe les mots selon ce que tu vois écrit: 'in' ou 'un'. Ne lis pas encore.

description: Child confuses 'oi' and 'ou' in reading — reading 'voix' as 'voux' or 'mois' as 'mous'. Both are complex vowel graphemes. Exercise uses picture anchors — each vowel grapheme is paired with a keyword picture (oi = oiseau, ou = ours) that the child recalls before reading any new word with that grapheme.
child_instruction: Rappelle-toi le mot-image. 'oi' comme oiseau, 'ou' comme ours. Lis le mot.

description: Child substitutes vowels and omits syllables simultaneously — reducing polysyllabic words with vowel errors. Exercise isolates each problem separately before combining: first syllable count check, then vowel accuracy check, then full reading.
child_instruction: Vérifie le nombre de syllabes, puis les voyelles, puis lis.

description: Child confuses the graphemes 'an' and 'en' in reading — both produce the same nasal sound /ɑ̃/ but appear in different words. Child reads 'enfant' as 'anfant' or 'lentement' as 'lantement'. Exercise builds grapheme awareness through word family sorting — child classifies words by their nasal grapheme (an vs en) by colour coding, then reads each group aloud without relying on sound alone.
child_instruction: Colorie les mots en 'an' en bleu et les mots en 'en' en rouge. Puis lis-les.

description: Child confuses all nasal vowel graphemes — an/en/in/on — producing inconsistent readings. Exercise builds a visual classification chart — child sorts words under the correct nasal vowel before reading the complete list aloud.
child_instruction: Classe les mots dans le bon groupe, puis lis-les.

description: Child substitutes vowels specifically in unstressed syllables of three-syllable words — reading 'salade' as 'selade', 'cadeau' as 'cedeau', or 'malade' as 'melade'. Exercise uses stress marking — child taps the stressed syllable first, then reads from the beginning applying correct vowels to unstressed positions. Tapping the stress anchor before reading helps the child maintain vowel quality throughout the word.
child_instruction: Tape la syllabe forte. Maintenant lis depuis le début avec les bonnes voyelles.

description: Child confuses the vowel graphemes eu and ou — reading 'feu' as 'fou', 'peur' as 'pour', or 'bleu' as 'blou'. This confusion is particularly disruptive because it changes word meaning completely. Exercise uses semantic verification — child reads a sentence containing an eu/ou target word, checks whether it makes sense, and self-corrects using the sentence context as feedback.
child_instruction: Lis la phrase. Est-ce que le mot souligné a du sens? Corrige si nécessaire.

description: Child substitutes vowels in multisyllabic words with complex vowel graphemes like eau/au/o — reading 'bateau' as 'batou'. Exercise builds grapheme-phoneme correspondence charts and uses timed fluency passages.
child_instruction: Lis le mot. Quelle lettre ou groupe de lettres fait ce son?

description: Child confuses 'ai' and 'ei' graphemes in reading — both produce /ɛ/ but child reads 'neige' with the 'ai' sound pattern or 'fait' with 'ei' sound. Exercise builds grapheme inventory — child creates a personal reference chart of all graphemes producing /ɛ/ (ai, ei, è, ê, e+consonant) before reading target words.
child_instruction: Retrouve toutes les façons d'écrire le son /ɛ/ sur ta carte. Puis lis les mots.

description: Child makes vowel substitution errors specifically under reading speed pressure — correct at slow pace but errors increase at normal speed. Exercise uses paced reading with a metronome — child reads at 20% below natural speed, gradually increasing pace while maintaining vowel accuracy.
child_instruction: Lis en rythme avec le métronome. On augmente la vitesse quand tu es prêt(e).

description: Child misreads words where silent letters interact with vowel graphemes — reading 'beaucoup' incorrectly because of the sequence eau+ou+p, or 'automne' because of au+mn. At DIFF=5, the child must navigate multiple overlapping grapheme-phoneme rules simultaneously. Exercise builds rule-stacking awareness — child annotates each grapheme group before reading, then reads the full word applying all rules at once.
child_instruction: Entoure chaque groupe de lettres qui fait un seul son. Puis lis le mot entier.

description: Child confuses vowel graphemes in academic vocabulary — reading 'équation' with wrong vowels, or 'scientifique' with vowel substitutions in medial syllables. Exercise targets content-area reading — child pre-reads key vocabulary from a science or history text, annotating vowel graphemes before reading the full passage.
child_instruction: Avant de lire le texte, annote les voyelles complexes dans les mots soulignés.

description: Severe vowel substitution pattern affecting all vowel categories simultaneously — child has not consolidated any vowel grapheme-phoneme mappings reliably. Exercise uses cumulative review — one new vowel grapheme is practiced to mastery each week; exercise presents all mastered graphemes together in a mixed reading set.
child_instruction: Utilise ta liste de voyelles maîtrisées. Lis chaque mot et vérifie.

description: Child substitutes vowels in written production as well as reading — errors are bidirectional. Exercise integrates reading and spelling — child reads a word, spells it aloud letter by letter emphasizing the vowel grapheme, then writes it from memory. Bidirectional reinforcement builds orthographic memory.
child_instruction: Lis → épelle à voix haute (insiste sur la voyelle) → écris de mémoire.
